page: Amazon Web Services c8id.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, delivering 16 virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning includes 32.0 GB of high-frequency 7 GHz DDR5 RAM, equating to 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware acceleration includes Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8) alongside AVX-512 instruction sets with bfloat16 and VNNI support. Integrated storage includes a 950 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, complemented by an 8 Gbps baseline network capability. No GPUs are attached to this instance type.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates elevated single-threaded capability, placing in the top quartile for Geekbench single-core scores (2219.0) as well as compression metrics such as single-threaded gzip (34.49 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.44 GB/sec). Natural language processing execution is notably responsive, marked by top-decile Geekbench text processing and small-model (135M) LLM text generation rates reaching 390.86 tokens per second. Multi-core operations show solid middle-tier throughput, registered at 17,299.69 on stress-ng and 13,435.0 on Geekbench multi-core. PassMark CPU execution reached 29,256.57, with memory bandwidth benchmarks recording 136.59 GB/sec on large block uncached reads and 71.98 GB/sec on writes.

Qualitatively, the compute-to-memory ratio of 1:2 makes c8id.4xlarge resource-efficient for workloads prioritizing raw clock speeds and vector calculation over large memory allocations. The inclusion of low-latency direct-attached NVMe storage minimizes auxiliary block storage overhead for temporary scratch operations. These architectural attributes make the instance suitable for CPU-bound tasks, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch data transformations, media compression, and caching services requiring rapid local disk staging.

The instance features a 16-vCPU, 8-physical-core Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor clocked at 3.9 GHz, paired with 32.0 GB of 7 GHz DDR5 memory and bundled with a 950 GB NVMe SSD local volume. Network throughput is rated at an 8 Gbps baseline. Compute testing indicates strong single-threaded throughput, placing in the top quartile for single-core Geekbench performance and compression tasks, with top-tier results in text processing and small-model text generation. Multi-threaded and memory bandwidth metrics reflect balanced mid-range capacity. The hardware profile lacks dedicated GPU acceleration and maintains a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio, offering efficient resource utilization for CPU-bound computation, software compilation, batch processing, and workloads requiring fast temporary local storage.
